claim: When a request is blocked the proxy responds 403 with x-proxy-error set to one of blocked-by-allowlist, blocked-by-denylist, blocked-by-method-policy, or blocked-by-policy.
explanation: blocked_header_value also emits blocked-by-mitm-hook and blocked-by-mitm-required (responses.rs:57-58), which are not in the documented list of possible values.

claim: Launcher environment payloads are limited to 1,000,000 UTF-8 bytes and chunks to 4096 bytes.
explanation: mxc-sandbox transport.rs delegates to codex_windows_sandbox::environment_transport, which uses CHUNK_BYTES = 16 KiB and MAX_BYTES = 16 MiB. No 1,000,000-byte or 4096-byte limit exists anywhere in the mxc-sandbox crate.

claim: If system bwrap is present but too old to support --argv0, the helper keeps using system bubblewrap with a no-argv0 compatibility path.
explanation: A system bwrap is only kept if its --help output advertises --as-pid-1 (line 212) and --perms (system_bwrap_launcher_for_path_with_probe requires supports_perms: true, line 173). Older builds that lack either option are silently rejected and the bundled bwrap is used instead, so the no-argv0 path applies only to bwrap that has those flags but lacks --argv0.

claim: bytes header values no longer work: passing bytes as a header value now raises an error
explanation: build_headers only checks for `Omit` and then does `headers[name] = value` on an httpx2.Headers, which accepts bytes. Nothing in the SDK type-checks or rejects non-str header values (a grep for such a check found none). The only bytes-related TypeError is for `body=` (line 676). bytes header values are not rejected, except possibly by an AttributeError on the x-stainless-helper path. I did not run this, and I did not inspect httpx2's own Headers implementation.

claim: Realtime API: no errors are raised directly by the SDK when an `error` event comes in; the connection stays usable and you must handle it yourself.
explanation: When using the connection's dispatch_events() loop with no handler registered for "error" or "event", the SDK raises OpenAIError("WebSocket error: ...") for an incoming RealtimeErrorEvent (sync path likewise at line 928 for the other connection class). So the 'no errors raised directly' promise only holds for plain iteration.

claim: The token refresh buffer defaults to 1200 seconds (20 minutes) before expiration.
explanation: The configured or default buffer (1200s) is clamped with min(configured_buffer, expires_in / 2). For tokens with a lifetime under 40 minutes the effective refresh buffer is less than 1200 seconds, and a user-supplied refresh_buffer_seconds is also silently clamped to half the token lifetime.

claim: A header entry in default_headers, extra_headers, with_options or ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS replaces a header of the same name whatever its casing, including the headers the SDK sets itself
explanation: build_headers special-cases `x-stainless-helper` (_APPEND_HEADERS). A later layer does not replace it. Its value is appended to the earlier value as a comma-separated, de-duplicated list. Every other header is replaced as documented.

claim: Web browsers: disabled by default; enable by explicitly setting dangerouslyAllowBrowser to true.
explanation: For AzureOpenAI, supplying an azureADTokenProvider silently turns browser use on unless the caller passes an explicit false. Only the internal security-model doc mentions this; README and azure docs do not.

claim: authToken defaults to the ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN environment variable.
explanation: The provider reads authToken only from options. Without it, it falls back to ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. The repo's own example passes process.env.ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN by hand, and the provider source never references the variable.

claim: Non-http(s) schemes are rejected when fetching a URL taken from a provider response.
explanation: validateDownloadUrl returns early for `data:` URLs and only rejects other non-http(s) schemes. The docs say non-http(s) schemes are rejected without mentioning this exception.

claim: The Google Cloud client never reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN or ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL; it authenticates with Google credentials only
explanation: The constructor calls Anthropic.__init__, which does read ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN when none is passed (the comment at lines 335-338 says so). The client then overwrites api_key and auth_token with None, and passes base_url "" so the parent skips ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. The values are read but never used for auth or the URL, so the promise holds in effect but not literally.

claim: OIDC token renewal failures delay further exchange attempts by one second, doubling after each failure up to 30 seconds.
explanation: MAX_RENEWAL_BACKOFF is Duration::from_secs(61), and the delay is computed as (previous * 2).min(MAX_RENEWAL_BACKOFF) at auth.rs:252. The sequence is 1,2,4,8,16,32,61 seconds, so the cap is 61 seconds, not the documented 30.

claim: Retries are opt in. The SDK does not retry general model requests unless you set ModelSettings(retry=...) and your retry policy chooses to retry.
explanation: With no retry settings, _should_disable_provider_managed_retries returns False on the initial attempt (and on later attempts when there is no policy), so the underlying OpenAI client's built-in retries stay active. The code comments say provider retries are the only transient-failure recovery in that case. Model requests are therefore retried by default; only the runner-managed retry layer is opt-in.

claim: Realtime WebSocket transport_config max_size: the SDK default is None, leaving incoming message size unlimited.
explanation: The realtime connection always starts with connect_kwargs max_size set to 8 * 1024 * 1024 and only overrides it if transport_config supplies max_size. The default is therefore an 8 MiB limit, not unlimited. (The unlimited default is true only for the Responses websocket transport, which sets max_size None.)

claim: Supported operating systems are macOS 12+, Ubuntu 20.04+/Debian 10+, or Windows 11 via WSL2.
explanation: The repo ships a native Windows installer and release targets (x86_64/aarch64-pc-windows-msvc), plus native Windows sandbox backends (windows-sandbox-rs, mxc-sandbox). Windows is not limited to WSL2 as the table implies.

claim: OpenAI compaction items are returned as text parts with special providerMetadata and sent back as compaction input items.
explanation: Round-tripping works, but compaction items come back as `custom` content parts with kind openai.compaction, not as `text` parts.

claim: Caller headers (Authorization, Cookie, provider API-key headers) are not sent to a host on a different origin than the provider's.
explanation: fetchWithValidatedRedirects only sanitizes risky headers on the first request. It still sends Authorization and custom API-key headers to whatever origin the response-supplied URL points to, and drops them only on a later cross-origin redirect. Only the opt-in fetchUntrustedUrl isolates credentials on the first hop. The same page admits this at line 81, which contradicts the unconditional claim at line 41.
